goal: Prevent memory amplification denial-of-service risks from specially crafted witness stacks
Reduce worst-case transaction memory footprint to fit more transactions in the mempool
reviewability: PR is ready to review with all requested changes incorporated and no pending items
agreement: Strong support for mitigating persistent memory usage and DoS risks (instagibbs, optout21)
Verified via serialization roundtrips, span lifetimes, and disassembly comparisons (l0rinc)
Initial concerns on vector limits and materialization were addressed or deferred (optout21, l0rinc, brunoerg)
Concept approval without stated reasons (w0xlt, darosior, xyzconstant)

categories.name: mempool
why: P1 because it removes an amplification denial-of-service attack on mempool and orphanage memory
Worst-case memory drops from roughly 28 bytes per weight unit down to 1.6
Allows standard mempool limits to store 13-15% more transactions under adversarial conditions

categories.name: validation
why: P2 because it protects node validation structures against adversarial heap expansion
Touches consensus and script execution paths across validation code
Introduces minor worst-case block validation overhead that warrants careful performance review
